result.title: ARC-VLN: Adaptive Recursive Computing-based Visual-Language Navigation
result.summary: Efficient aerial visual-language navigation (VLN) requires reducing model storage and inference costs while maintaining instruction-conditioned action prediction. We present ARC-VLN, a token-type-aware recursive computation framework built on a language backbone with shared parameters. ARC-VLN retains full-depth computation for text and action tokens while adaptively selecting exit depths for visual tokens. Representations of early-exiting visual tokens are retained, and active-token compaction shortens the sequences processed by subsequent recursive blocks. To mitigate routing collapse to a single exit depth, we design a dedicated learning strategy that encourages the model to distribute visual tokens across multiple exit depths.On OpenFly's Test-Seen and Test-Unseen subsets, ARC-VLN achieves the lowest navigation error and the highest success rate and success weighted by path length among all compared methods. Meanwhile, it reduces the average number of decision steps per trajectory, total floating-point operations, mean model inference time per trajectory, and average GPU memory usage during inference, indicating its great potential as a VLN backbone for lightweight applications.

AI.brief_summary: ARC-VLN 面向空中视觉语言导航，提出按 token 类型区分的递归计算框架：文本与动作 token 走完整深度，视觉 token 自适应选择退出深度并保留其表示，配合 active-token compaction 缩短后续序列，并用专门训练策略缓解路由坍缩到单一深度。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接处理视觉 token 与语言 token 间的动态算力分配及共享参数递归块，可作为「视觉证据需要多深处理」「LOOK 的算力成本」的对照线索，也可核查视觉 token 早退后其表示是否仍被动作预测实际使用。
